title: Records Retention Schedule
subtitle: Health and safety records, Gqeberha plant, approved 3 August 2026

blocks.p: This schedule sets, for every type of health and safety record we keep, why we keep it, where it is held, who may see it, how long we keep it and how we dispose of it. The Health and Safety Manager, Busisiwe Tshabalala, reviews it every year and whenever the law or our operations change.

Many of these records hold personal information about our employees, contractors and visitors. Under the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), we collect and keep this information only to meet our health and safety duties under the OHS Act and COIDA and to protect the people on our site. We keep it for the period the applicable regulations set, or the practitioner sets where no regulation sets one, and no longer; restrict access to the people named below, keep it secure and dispose of it safely. Medical records are held by the occupational health practitioner; our File holds only the fitness outcome (fit, fit with restrictions, unfit). Employees may ask to see their own records by writing to the Information Officer, Ruan de Villiers.

**How the retention column works.** Where regulations set how long a record type is kept, the column says **as the applicable regulations set**, and the registered Health and Safety practitioner confirms which regulations apply to our agents, equipment and activities. Records of exposure to hazardous agents and of medical surveillance are kept for the long periods those regulations set, because disease from an exposure can appear many years later. **As the practitioner sets** is used only for record types no regulation covers.

bullets: Paper records are kept in locked cabinets; only the people in the access column hold keys.
Electronic records are kept in folders with access limited to the same people, and the server is backed up.
No record is destroyed while an inspection, claim, investigation or legal matter about it is open.
Every disposal is recorded in the disposal log: record type, dates covered, method, date and the person who did it.
